rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Aṭāʾ says asking a young person for one's needs is easier than asking the old, as Joseph readily pardoned his brothers while Jacob deferred forgiveness.
rows.anchor: طلب الحوائج إلى الشاب أسهل منها في الشيوخ

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الملاني الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reads Jacob's promise as asking Joseph to forgive the brothers first, after which Joseph would seek God's forgiveness for them.
rows.anchor: أسأل يوسف إن عفا عنكم استغفر لكم ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jacob asked the bearer how Joseph was left; learning Joseph ruled Egypt and remained Muslim, Jacob said the blessing was now complete.
rows.anchor: على أي دين تركته؟ قال: على دين الإسلام. فقال يعقوب: الآن تمت النعمة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān reports that Jacob and Joseph embraced and wept; Joseph wondered why Jacob mourned when resurrection would reunite them, and Jacob feared loss of Joseph's faith.
rows.anchor: ولكن خشيت أن تسلب دينك، فيحال بيني وبينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph sent supplies and two hundred camels, then went with Egypt's king and four thousand troops to meet Jacob; Judah led Jacob's mount, and Jacob mistook Joseph for Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: بعث مع البشير إلى يعقوب جهازا ومائتي راحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph was prevented from greeting first because Jacob had greater right and merit; Jacob greeted him as the one who had gone away with sorrows.
rows.anchor: وكان يعقوب أحق بذلك منه وأفضل، فابتدأه يعقوب بالسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation to enter Egypt was spoken while Joseph met his family before they entered the country, resolving why the verse reports it after their arrival.
rows.anchor: قال لهم هذا القول حين تلقاهم قبل دخولهم مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation rearranges the verse so God's will qualifies Jacob's promise to seek forgiveness; this is attributed to Abū Jarīr.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستثناء من قول يعقوب حين قال: سوف أستغفر لكم ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation attaches the conditional to the family's safety, not to entering Egypt, comparing it with the promise of safe entry into the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: إنما وقع الاستثناء على الأمن لا على الدخول

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says Joseph was separated from Jacob for 220 years.
rows.anchor: فقال الكلبي: مائتان وعشرون سنة

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: Salmān al-Fārisī gives the separation as forty years.
rows.anchor: سلمان الفارسي: أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād gives the separation as seventy years.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن شداد: سبعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported chronology gives the separation as seventy-seven years.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سبع وسبعون سنة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Joseph entered the well at seventeen, was away from his father eighty years, lived another twenty-three after reunion, and died aged 120.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: ألقي يوسف في الجب وهو ابن سبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah's chronology gives Joseph's age at death as 126 years.
rows.anchor: وفي التوراة: مائة وست وعشر سنين

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق بن يسار
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq ibn Yasār gives the separation as eighty-seven years.
rows.anchor: في قول ابن إسحاق بن يسار: ثمانين وسبعة أعوام

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq gives the separation as eighteen years.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي إسحاق: ثماني عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says God brought him out of prison rather than the well as a gracious way to avoid recalling his brothers' offense.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل من الجب استعمالا للكرم لئلا يذكر إخوته صنيعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation says rescue from prison was the greater blessing: the well followed his brothers' envy, while prison repaid a lapse of Joseph's.
rows.anchor: نعمة الله عليه في النجاة من السجن أكبر من نعمته عليه في إنقاذه من الجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob and his sons had lived as Bedouin herders; al-badw is the verbal noun of becoming a desert-dweller.
rows.anchor: كانوا أهل بادية ومواشي، والبدو مصدر قولك: بدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's incitement means that he corrupted relations between Joseph and his brothers.
rows.anchor: من بعد أن نزغ أفسد الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Latīf describes God as acting with subtle kindness as He wills and knowing the fine details and realities of things.
rows.anchor: لطيف ذو لطف وصنع لما يشاء عالم بدقائق الأمور وحقائقها

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb reports that Jacob's group entered Egypt as 72 men and women; with Moses, 600,570 men left, besides dependents, and descendants numbered 1.2 million besides fighters.
rows.anchor: قال: دخلوا- يعني يعقوب وولده- مصر وهم اثنان وسبعون إنسانا

rows.speaker: أهل التاريخ
rows.claim: Historians say Jacob lived twenty-four prosperous years in Egypt, died there, and asked Joseph to bury him beside Isaac in Syria; Joseph did so and returned.
rows.anchor: أقام يعقوب بمصر بعد موافاته بأهله أربعا وعشرين سنة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Jacob was carried in a teak coffin to Jerusalem and buried with Esau, who died the same day; both twins lived 147 years.
rows.anchor: نقل في تابوت من ساج إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd explains that some Jews transport their dead to Jerusalem because Jacob was buried there.
rows.anchor: فمن ثم تنقل اليهود موتاهم إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is unseen news revealed to Muhammad; he was absent when Jacob's sons agreed to cast Joseph into the well and plotted against him.
rows.anchor: وما كنت يا محمد عند أولاد يعقوب إذ أجمعوا أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people will not believe even if Muhammad is eager for their faith.
rows.anchor: وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت على إيمانهم بمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad asks no payment or reward for conveying the message and calling people to God; the Qur'an is only a reminder for all worlds.
rows.anchor: من أجر: جعل وجزاء إن هو يعني القرآن والوحي إلا ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many signs in heaven and earth are admonitions, lessons, and proofs, yet people pass them without reflection or taking heed.
rows.anchor: وكم قول فيه عظة وعبرة ودلالة في السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥārith ibn Qudāma transmits ʿIkrima's nominative reading of wa-l-arḍu yamurrūna ʿalayhā.
rows.anchor: الحرث بن قدامة عن عكرمة أنه قرأ: والأرض يمرون عليها رفعا

rows.speaker: عمرو بن وائل
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar heard ʿAmr ibn Wāʾil read the heavenly signs with qaṭʿan and wa-l-arḍu in the nominative.
rows.anchor: سمعت عمرو بن وائل يقرأ: وكأين من آية في السماوات قطعا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī is reported to read wa-l-arḍa in the accusative and to read yamurrūna ʿalā al-arḍ.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: أنه قرأ والأرض يمرون عليها نصبا، وقرأ: يمرون على الأرض

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Sufyān transmits ʿAbd Allāh's reading, wa-kāʾin min āyatin fī al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi yamshūna ʿalayhā.
rows.anchor: قال: وقرأ عبد الله: وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمشون عليها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima explains that the polytheists acknowledge God created heaven and earth and sends rain, yet still associate others with Him.
rows.anchor: من خلق السماوات والأرض؟ قالوا: الله، وإذا سئلوا من نزل القطر

rows.speaker: عكرمة وعامر
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and ʿĀmir say they believe God is their Lord and creator while associating others beneath Him; al-Thaʿlabī calls this the majority exegetes' view.
rows.anchor: يؤمنون بالله أنه ربهم وهو خالقهم ويشركون من دونه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about Arab polytheists' pilgrimage chants, which affirmed God's uniqueness and then added a partner owned by God; several tribes had variant chants.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يقولون في تلبيتهم: لبيك لا شريك لك إلا شريك هو لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another occasion says the polytheists heard the preceding signs, professed belief in their Creator, but claimed He had a partner, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: قالوا: فإنا نؤمن بالله الذي خلق هذه الأشياء ولكنا نزعم أن له شريكا

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ applies the verse to supplication: unbelievers associate partners in ease but sincerely invoke God in distress.
rows.anchor: أشركوا بربهم في الرخاء، فإذا أصابهم البلاء أخلصوا في الدعاء

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Some scholars of meaning read the phrase as saying that most people believed in God only after previously being polytheists, like the earlier nation described as stronger.
rows.anchor: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون قبل إيمانهم

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb applies the verse to the smoke during Mecca's drought: people prayed for relief and professed belief, then reverted to unbelief when punishment lifted; return presupposes an earlier state.
rows.anchor: عودهم إلى الكفر بعد كشف العذاب بيانه قوله: إنكم عائدون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses a gāshiya as something enveloping them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: مجللة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses the gāshiya as a punishment that covers them.
rows.anchor: مجاهِد: عذاب يغشاهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda glosses the enveloping punishment as a calamity; al-Ḍaḥḥāk specifies lightning and devastating strikes.
rows.anchor: قتادة: وقيعة، الضحاك: يعني الصواعق والقوارع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Hour may arrive as a cry that overtakes people in their marketplaces.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: تصيح الصيحة بالناس وهم في أسواقهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the Prophet's way as his Sunna and method.
rows.anchor: سبيلِي سنتي ومنهاجي، قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ explains the Prophet's way as his invitation.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع: دعوتي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains the Prophet's way as his supplication.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: دعائي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil explains the Prophet's way as his religion.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited command to call in God's way with wisdom equates God's way with His religion.
rows.anchor: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة أي دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being upon insight means acting with certainty; one who is mustabṣir is sure about the matter.
rows.anchor: على يقين، يقال: فلان مستبصر في كذا أي مستيقن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says those who believe in and affirm the Prophet also call people to God.
rows.anchor: آمن بي وصدقني فهو أيضا يدعو إلى الله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says followers must call people to what the Prophet called, remind them with Qur'an and admonition, and forbid disobedience.
rows.anchor: أحق والله على من اتبعه أن يدعو إلي بما دعا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the phrase to mean that the Prophet and everyone who follows him are all upon insight.
rows.anchor: معناه أنا ومن اتبعني على بصيرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes Muhammad's Companions as following the best course and soundest guidance, repositories of knowledge and faith, and God's army.
rows.anchor: كانوا على أحسن طريقة وأقصد هداية، معدن العلم، وكنز الإيمان وجند الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to glorify God is a declaration that He is exalted above the partners ascribed to Him.
rows.anchor: أي وقل: سبحان الله تنزيها له عما أشركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent human men, not angels, as messengers, from the towns rather than the desert, whose inhabitants the author deems more rational, virtuous, learned, and forbearing.
rows.anchor: إلا رجالا لا ملائكة، نوحي إليهم من أهل القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are urged to travel and learn how earlier rejecting peoples ended, so they may take heed.
rows.anchor: أخبر بأمر الأمم المكذبة من قبلهم، فيعتبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better for the God-fearing; the unstated point is that God saves His obedient allies when punishment arrives.
rows.anchor: هذا فعلنا في الدنيا بأهل ولايتنا وطاعتنا أن ننجيهم عند نزول العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it the abode of the Hereafter is an honorific construction, like saying true certainty, the former year, or the last spring.
rows.anchor: وأضيف الدار إلى الآخرة ولا خلاف لتعظيمها كقوله تعالى: إن هذا لهو حق اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic line uses the expression to mean certain knowledge and illustrates the commentary's discussion of the genitive construction.
rows.anchor: ولو أقوت عليك ديار عبس … عرفت الذل عرفان اليقين

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب، ابن عباس، ابن مسعود، أبي بن كعب، وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: These authorities read kuddhibū with a light dāl; the reading is also attributed to many later reciters and was chosen by al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayda.
rows.anchor: فقرأها قوم بالتخفيف وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: عائشة، الأعرج، نافع، الزهري، عطاء بن أبي رياح
rows.claim: A light reading is also reported from the Prophet and from these named readers, followed by Qatāda, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĪsā, Sallām, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, and Yaʿqūb.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قرأ وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا مخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the light reading, the apostles despair of their people's faith and the people think the apostles lied about the promised punishment.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ بالتخفيف، فمعناه: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل من إيمان قومهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains the light reading to a Qurashī youth: the messengers despaired of their people believing them, while the recipients thought the messengers had lied.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل من قومهم أن يصدقوهم، وظن المرسل إليهم أن الرسل كذبوهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk praised Saʿīd for answering a difficult reading and said traveling to Yemen to learn this interpretation would be little effort.
rows.anchor: لو رحلت في هذه إلى اليمن لكان قليلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also said to read the light form as the messengers despairing and thinking they had been let down; the account continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وهذه رواية ابن أبي مليكة عن ابن عباس قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās's interpretation, the messengers and believers prayed, weakened, despaired, and thought they had been delayed; the verse echoes the believers' cry for aid.
rows.anchor: كانوا دعوا فضعفوا ويئسوا وظنوا أنهم أخلفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the doubled reading, one interpretation has messengers despairing of their people's belief and knowing with certainty that their nations denied them; this is Qatāda's view.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل من قومهم أن يؤمنوا بهم وظنت الرسل أي استيقنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another doubled-reading interpretation says messengers feared that believers had recanted because rescue was delayed; this is attributed to ʿĀʾisha.
rows.anchor: وظنت الرسل أن من قد آمن بهم وصدقوهم قد كذبوهم فارتدوا عن دينهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reads the consonants with open kāf and dhāl; one gloss says the messengers despaired of punishing their people while the people thought the messengers lied.
rows.anchor: قرأ مجاهد كذبوا بفتح الكاف والذال مخففة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid's other gloss has messengers despairing of their people's faith and knowing that the people, through unbelief, falsely charged God.
rows.anchor: وظنت الرسل أن قومهم قد كذبوا على الله بكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saves the obedient believers when punishment descends, and His punishment cannot be turned away from criminal polytheists.
rows.anchor: فنجي من نشاء عند نزول العذاب وهم المطيعون والمؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use two nūns for fanunajjī; al-Kisāʾī assimilates one, while ʿĀṣim reads a passive form with one nūn, a doubled jīm, and fatḥa on yāʾ.
rows.anchor: فقرأها عامة القراء فننجي بنونين على معنى فنحن نفعل بهم ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd prefers ʿĀṣim's passive reading because it appears in the ʿUthmānic and regional codices.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد هذه القراءة لأنها في مصحف عثمان

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads fanajā as a light past-tense verb; the subject is nominative with ʿĀṣim's and his reading, but accusative with the others.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن فنجا من نشاء بفتح النون والتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Joseph and his brothers teaches a lesson to people of understanding; the Qur'an is not fabricated but confirms prior scripture, explains what people need, and guides and shows mercy to believers.
rows.anchor: لقد كان في قصصهم أي في خبر يوسف وأخوته عبرة عظة لأولي الألباب

rows.speaker: طلحة بن عبيد الله
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh reports that the Prophet defined subḥān Allāh as declaring God free of every evil.
rows.anchor: تنزيه الله عن كل سوء

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse uses subḥān to express wonder.
rows.anchor: أقول لما جاءني فخر … سبحان من علقمة الفاخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse carries both meanings of subḥān: wonder and God's freedom from evil.
rows.anchor: فالآية متضمنة للمعنيين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the Night Journey began at Mecca's mosque; the Prophet's report places him in the Ḥijr beside the Kaʿba between sleep and wakefulness when Gabriel brought the Buraq.
rows.anchor: كان أسراء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من مسجد مكة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying he was in the Sacred Mosque, in the Ḥijr by the Kaʿba, between sleeping and waking when Gabriel came with the Buraq.
rows.anchor: بينما أنا في المسجد الحرام في الحجر عند البيت بين النائم واليقظان

rows.speaker: أم هانئ
rows.claim: Another view places the start at Umm Hāniʾ's home; its proponents say the Sacred Mosque means the whole sanctuary, which is all treated as a mosque.
rows.anchor: معنى قوله من المسجد الحرام من الحرم، لأن الحرم كله مسجد

rows.speaker: أم هانئ
rows.claim: Umm Hāniʾ says the Prophet prayed Fajr with her after his Night Journey and explained that Gabriel had come to him at his prayer place.
rows.anchor: فقلت: كل حديثك العجب بأبي أنت وأمي فقام وصلى الغداة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil dates the Night Journey to one year before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: كانت ليلة الإسراء قبل الهجرة بسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Masjid al-Aqṣā means Jerusalem, the farthest mosque visited.
rows.anchor: يعني بيت المقدس، سمي أقصى لأنه أبعد المساجد التي تزار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God blessed the area around Jerusalem with water, rivers, trees, and fruits.
rows.anchor: باركنا حوله بالماء والأنهار والأشجار والثمار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says Jerusalem is blessed because it is where prophets stayed, angels and revelation descended, the Rock stands, and people will be gathered.
rows.anchor: مقر الأنبياء، وفيه مهبط الملائكة والوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs shown to the Prophet were wonders of God's power; God is hearing and seeing.
rows.anchor: لنريه من آياتنا عجائب أمرنا إنه هو السميع البصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says he selected famous transmitted Night Journey reports, excluding objectionable and weak-chain accounts, and arranged them concisely for ease and benefit.
rows.anchor: اقتصرت به على الأخبار المأثورة المشهورة دون المناكير والأحاديث الواهية الأسانيد

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: The author begins a report from Jābir about the Prophet's Night Journey, followed by a composite report transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: روى الزهري عن ابن سلمة بن عبد الرحمن قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله يقول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through Ibn ʿAbbās begins with the Prophet's chest being opened, washed three times with Zamzam, filled with wisdom, knowledge, and faith, and sealed with the prophetic mark.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: دخل كلام بعضهم في بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Ibn ʿAbbās Prophetic report, Gabriel gives the Prophet water from Zamzam and Kawthar, then brings a Buraq, described as between a donkey and mule, swift as a glance and adorned with precious materials.
rows.anchor: فإذا أنا بالبراق- دابة فوق الحمار ودون البغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Buraq initially balks; Gabriel rebukes it, saying no prophet more honored by God than Muhammad has ever ridden it, and it lowers itself in shame.
rows.anchor: ما ركبك مذ كنت قط نبي أكرم على الله من محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the route, a Jewish caller urges Muhammad to stop; Gabriel says accepting would have made his community Jewish, and a Christian caller's invitation would have made it Christian.
rows.anchor: داعية اليهود والذي نفسي بيده لو أجبته لتهودت أمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dazzling old woman represents the world; Gabriel says that if Muhammad turned toward her, his community would choose this life over the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فهي الدنيا لو التويت إليها لاختارت أمتك الدنيا على الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet chooses milk over wine; Gabriel calls this the fitra for him and his community and says choosing wine would lead the community astray.
rows.anchor: فأخذت اللبن فشربته. فقال لي جبرئيل: أصبت الفطرة أنت وأمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People whose crops regrow immediately after harvest represent those who migrate in God's path; their good deeds multiply seven hundredfold, and their spending is replaced by God.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء المهاجرون في سبيل الله يضاعف لهم الحسنة سبعمائة ضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People whose heads are repeatedly crushed by stones represent those who neglect the prescribed prayers.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الذين تتثاقل رؤوسهم عن الصلاة المكتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those driven like cattle with rags on front and back represent people who withhold alms; the report says God did not wrong them.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الذين لا يؤدون صدقات أموالهم ما ظلمهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man and woman who leave their lawful spouses for illicit partners represent adulterers and adulteresses.
rows.anchor: هذا الرجل من يكون عنده المرأة حلالا طيبا فأتى امرأة خبيثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman who tears every garment or object on the road represents people who waylay others, as in the prohibition against sitting on every path to threaten.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل أمتك يقعدون على الطريق فيقطعون بمثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man unable to carry a large bundle who keeps adding to it represents someone burdened with trusts he cannot discharge but accepts more.
rows.anchor: هذا الرجل من أمتك عليه أمانات الناس لا يقدر على أدائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preachers of discord are represented by people whose tongues and lips are repeatedly cut with iron shears.
rows.anchor: قال هؤلاء خطباء الفتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An enormous ox emerging from a small stone represents someone who speaks a grave word, regrets it, and cannot retract it.
rows.anchor: يتكلم الكلمة العظيمة ثم يندم عليها ولا يستطيع أن يردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pleasant cool scent and sound belong to Paradise, which asks God for what He promised amid its abundant furnishings, fabrics, and foods.
rows.anchor: هذا صوت الجنة، فقال: رب أرني بما وعدتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell asks for what was promised, citing its chains, flames, boiling liquid, bitter food, and torments; God fills it with disbelievers, polytheists, wicked people, and tyrants who deny Judgment.
rows.anchor: لك كل مشرك ومشركة وكافر وكافرة وكل خبيث وخبيثة وكل جبار لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prays at Medina, Sinai, and Bethlehem, identified respectively with the future Hijra, God's speech to Moses, and Jesus's birth.
rows.anchor: صليت بطيبة وإليها المهاجرة إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Jerusalem, angels greet the Prophet as first, last, and gatherer; Gabriel says he is first resurrected and interceding, last of prophets, and that the gathering includes his community.
rows.anchor: إنك أول من تنشر عنه الأرض وعن أمتك، وأول شافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel ties the Buraq at the ring used by prophets and brings Muhammad into Jerusalem, where angels receive him with honor.
rows.anchor: وربط البراق بالحلقة الي كانت تربط بها الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad asks Gabriel who the assembled figures are; Gabriel identifies them as his brother prophets.
rows.anchor: يا جبرئيل من هؤلاء؟ قال: إخوتك الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel challenges claims by Quraysh, Jews, and Christians about partners or a son for God; the prophets affirm God's sole lordship, and Muhammad leads two units of prayer.
rows.anchor: زعمت قريش أن لله شريكا، واليهود والنصارى أن لله ولدا

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Abraham praises God for making him His intimate, granting great dominion, making him a leader, and rescuing him from the fire.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي اتخذني خليلا وأعطاني ملكا عظيما

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: Moses praises God for speaking to him, destroying Pharaoh through him, saving Israel through him, and giving his people a rightly guiding community.
rows.anchor: الذي كلمني تكليما وجعل هلاك فرعون منه ونجاة بني إسرائيل على يدي

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: David praises God for kingship, the Psalms, softened iron, mountains and birds praising with him, wisdom, and decisive speech.
rows.anchor: وألان لي الحديد وسخر لي الجبال يسبحن والطير

rows.speaker: سليمان
rows.claim: Solomon praises God for subjecting wind and demons, granting knowledge of birds, and giving him a great kingdom unlike any other and free of reckoning.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي سخر لي الرياح وسخر لي جنود الشياطين

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: Jesus praises God for making him a word, enabling miracles, raising him, purifying and protecting him and Mary from Satan.
rows.anchor: جعلني أخلق من الطين كهيئة الطير فأنفخ فيه فيكون طيرا بإذن الله

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muhammad praises God for sending him as mercy and universal warner, revealing the Qur'an, making his community best, balanced, first and last, and opening his chest and raising his mention.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي أرسلني رحمة للعالمين وكافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Abraham acknowledges that Muhammad has been favored over the assembled prophets.
rows.anchor: بهذا أفضلكم محمد، ثم أتى بآنية ثلاثة مغطاة أفواهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of three vessels, Muhammad takes water briefly, drinks milk to satisfaction, and declines wine; Gabriel says this was right because wine would be forbidden, few would follow him if he drank it, and excess water would overwhelm him and his community.
rows.anchor: فقال له جبرئيل: قد أصبت أما إنها ستحرم على أمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent stairway rises from Jerusalem's Rock; the report describes its beauty, gem-and-metal steps, and says angels ascend from it and the Angel of Death uses it.
rows.anchor: ومنه تعرج الملائكة أصله على صخرة بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel carries Muhammad to the first heaven, where the gatekeeper verifies Gabriel and Muhammad and welcomes them as brother and successor.
rows.anchor: حياه الله من أخ ومن خليفة فنعم الأخ ونعم الخليفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gigantic green-crested rooster in the lowest earth praises God beneath the Throne; its crowing makes earthly roosters answer in praise, and the Prophet longs to see it again.
rows.anchor: إذ رأيت ديكا له زغب أخضر ورأس أبيض

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that since seeing the great rooster he has longed to see it again.
rows.anchor: لم أزل منذ رأيت ذلك الديك مشتاقا إليه أن أراه ثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An angel whose body is half fire and half ice, neither overcoming the other, prays that God reconcile believers' hearts; named Ḥabīb, he is charged with the edges of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: ملك من الملائكة يقال له حبيب وكله الله بأكناف السماوات وأطراف الأرضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Angel of Death continuously views the tablet of creaturely lifespans and is the angels' hardest worker; he says the world and creatures are before him and his helpers identify those whose death is due.
rows.anchor: هذا ملك الموت دائب في قبض الأرواح وهو أشد الملائكة عملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Angel of Death says that when a soul reaches the throat he alone takes it, and no matter about his work is hidden from him.
rows.anchor: فإذا بلغ الروح الحلقوم علمت ذلك ولا يخفى علي شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mālik, keeper of Hell, has never smiled and grows angrier at God's enemies; at the Prophet's request he reveals a terrifying flame and smoke, which Gabriel closes after Muhammad nearly faints.
rows.anchor: هذا مالك خازن النار لم يتبسم قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet sees innumerable angels whose faces, mouths, and tongues fill their bodies, all praising God.
rows.anchor: منهم وجوه بين كتفيه ووجوه في صدره في كل وجه أفواه والسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam appears in full form between a Paradise gate and a Hell gate: he rejoices at descendants entering Paradise and weeps for those entering Hell.
rows.anchor: إذا نظر إلى من يدخل من ذريته الجنة ضحك واستبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel and Muhammad then ascend to the second heaven and are admitted.
rows.anchor: ثم صعدنا إلى السماء الثانية فاستفتح جبرئيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the second heaven Muhammad meets Jesus and John, described as maternal cousins.
rows.anchor: هذا عيسى ويحيى أبناء الخالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the third heaven he sees Joseph, whose beauty surpasses other people as the full moon surpasses the stars.
rows.anchor: هذا أخوك يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the fourth heaven he sees Enoch, whom God raised to a high station and who leans on the records of creatures' affairs.
rows.anchor: هذا إدريس رفعه الله مكانا عليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the seventh heaven, the angels welcome Muhammad as a brother and successor before admitting him.
rows.anchor: قالوا: حياه الله من أخ ومن خليفة، فنعم الأخ ونعم الخليفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the seventh heaven Muhammad enters and sees Abraham seated at the gate of Paradise.
rows.anchor: جالس على كرسي عند باب الجنة وعنده قوم جلوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is called the first person to grow gray; white-faced people never mixed faith with wrongdoing, while others mixed good and bad then repented and were forgiven.
rows.anchor: أول من شمط على الأرض، وأما هؤلاء البيض الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three rivers by Abraham represent God's mercy, blessing, and pure drink; beside him stands the Frequented House, entered daily by 70,000 angels who never return.
rows.anchor: هذا البيت المعمور يدخل فيه كل يوم سبعون ألف ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sidrat al-Muntahā has leaves covering the world and four rivers: two hidden in Paradise and two visible as the Nile and Euphrates; Paradise also has pure water, milk, wine, and honey rivers.
rows.anchor: وأما الظاهرين فالنيل والفرات ويخرج أيضا من أصلها أنهار

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet recognizes the Lote Tree's leaves and fruit; God's light and innumerable golden-looking angels overwhelm it, and Gabriel, stationed at its center, urges him onward.
rows.anchor: فلما انتهيت إليها قال لي جبرئيل: تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel tells Muhammad to advance because he is more honored; Muhammad approaches the golden screen while Gabriel remains behind, since it marks the end of creation.
rows.anchor: فإنك أكرم على الله مني، فتقدمت وجبرئيل على أثري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A guardian carries Muhammad through seventy screens, each five hundred years thick and separated by the same distance, then on a green couch to the Throne.
rows.anchor: حتى جاوزوا بي سبعين حجابا غلظ كل حجاب مسيرة خمسمائة عام

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At the Throne, a drop falls on Muhammad's tongue; after its sweetness and awe pass, God teaches him about earlier and later peoples and greets him in the prayer exchange.
rows.anchor: فقلت: التحيات لله والصلوات الطيبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says the Highest Assembly disputes over ranks and good deeds: ranks include thorough ablution in hardship, walking to congregational prayers, and waiting after one prayer; good deeds include greeting, feeding, and night prayer.
rows.anchor: الدرجات إسباغ الوضوء في المكروهات والمشي على الأقدام إلى الجماعات

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked about the Messenger and believers' faith, Muhammad affirms that they believe in God, angels, scriptures, and messengers without the distinctions made by Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: والمؤمنين كل آمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله لا نفرق بين أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts the believers' response of hearing and obeying and grants forgiveness, lifting accountability for forgetfulness, mistakes, and compulsion, as well as the requested protection and help.
rows.anchor: قد رفعت الخطأ والنسيان عنك وعن أمتك وما استكرهوا عليه

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muhammad asks how his honor compares with Abraham's friendship, Moses's speech, Enoch's elevation, Solomon's dominion, and David's Psalms.
rows.anchor: اتخذت إبراهيم خليلا، وكلمت موسى تكليما، ورفعت إدريس مكانا عليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers by making Muhammad His friend and speaking to him, granting the Opening and ending of al-Baqara from the Throne's treasures, and sending him universally to humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: وأعطيتك فاتحة الكتاب وخواتيم البقرة وكانا من كنوز العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes all land, dry or sea, a purifier and mosque for Muhammad's community, permits them the spoils unavailable to earlier nations, and grants victory through a month's-distance terror.
rows.anchor: وجعلت الأرض كلها برها وبحرها طهورا ومسجدا لك ولأمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God describes the Qur'an as the preeminent, confirming scripture, raises Muhammad's mention, grants him the Mathānī, Ḥawāmīm, and detailed chapters, and makes his community best, balanced, first, and last.
rows.anchor: وأنزلت عليك سيد الكتب كلها ومهيمنا عليها قرآنا فرقناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says God entrusted Muhammad with further matters he could not disclose and initially prescribed fifty daily prayers.
rows.anchor: ثم فرضت علي وعلى أمتي في كل يوم وليلة خمسون صلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel explains that the surrounding luminous canopies shield creation from the light of the Throne, beyond which lie still more astonishing creations.
rows.anchor: تلك سرادقات عرش رب العزة التي أحاطت بعرشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angelic ranks seen in the upper sea are spiritual angels, including the greatest Spirit; the foremost rank around the Throne consists of exalted Cherubim whom other angels dare not behold.
rows.anchor: هم الكروبيون أشراف الملائكة وعظمائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel tours Muhammad through Paradise's jeweled palaces, trees, rooms, rivers, and fruits; Muhammad says he knows each place there as well as his own mosque.
rows.anchor: فلأنا أعرف بكل قصر وبيت وغرفة وخيمة ونهر وثمر في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The river Kawthar, also called Tasnīm here, is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey; its waters flow among Paradise homes and flavor its drinks.
rows.anchor: هذا الكوثر الذي أعطاك الله عز وجل وهو التسنيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immense, fragrant, many-colored Tree of Ṭūbā bears every kind of fruit; many in Muhammad's community will rest eternally in its shade, and its delights are prepared for God's allies.
rows.anchor: ولكثير من أمتك ورهطك في ظلها حسن مقيل ونعيم طويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision of Paradise's reward prompts the Prophet to say that people should work for such a goal.
rows.anchor: لمثل هذا فليعمل العاملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People with camel-like lips forced to swallow burning stones represent those who consume orphans' wealth unjustly.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People with swollen bellies trampled by Pharaoh's followers represent usurers.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء أكلة الربا ومثلهم كمثل الذي يتخبطه الشيطان من المس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women hung by their breasts with heads down represent women who commit adultery and kill their children.
rows.anchor: هن اللاتي يزنين ويقتلن أولادهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses repeatedly urges Muhammad to seek a reduction from fifty prayers, saying his experience with Israel shows Muhammad's community is weaker; God reduces them to five, each counting tenfold, and says His decree remains fifty in reward.
rows.anchor: فرضت عليك وعلى أمتك خمسين صلوات، ولا يبدل القول لدي فخمسة بخمسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad accepts the five prayers, and Moses is portrayed as toughest when Muhammad first passed him but most compassionate when he returned.
rows.anchor: من أشدهم عليه حين مر به وخيرهم لهم حين رجع إليه

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The journey back to the Prophet's bed occurred in one night; he calls himself leader of Adam's descendants, bearer of the praise banner, and holder of Paradise's keys, without pride.
rows.anchor: وكان كل ذلك ليلة واحدة من لياليكم هذه فأنا سيد ولد آدم ولا فخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Dhū Ṭuwā the Prophet worries his people will disbelieve his account; Gabriel replies that Abū Bakr will believe him.
rows.anchor: يا جبرئيل إن قومي لا يصدقونني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿĀʾisha report that Muhammad woke in Mecca troubled, expecting people to deny that he had reached Jerusalem and returned overnight.
rows.anchor: عرفت إن الناس تكذبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jahl approaches the grieving Prophet mockingly, asks whether he benefited from anything, and then questions his claim to have gone to Jerusalem overnight.
rows.anchor: نعم إني أسري بي الليلة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: When told Muhammad claimed an overnight journey to Jerusalem, Abū Bakr says that if Muhammad said it, it is true, since he believes his more distant reports from heaven; this earns him the title al-Ṣiddīq.
rows.anchor: لئن كان قال ذلك لقد صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jahl summons Quraysh, whose members react with astonishment and disbelief; some believers apostatize after hearing the Prophet repeat his claim.
rows.anchor: فمن بين مصفق ومن بين واضع يده على رأسه متعجبا للكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travelers ask Muhammad to describe Jerusalem's mosque; he initially loses his train of description, then God displays it before him and the questioners confirm his account.
rows.anchor: فجيء بالمسجد وأنا أنظر إليه حتى وضع دون دار عقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh next asks about their caravan, saying it matters more to them than the account of the journey; the excerpt ends before Muhammad's reply.
rows.anchor: أخبرنا عن عيرنا فهي أهم إلينا من قولك
